card.title: MATILDA FROG
card.text: Deals double damage to infantry and HQ. Units to the left of this unit have +2 attack.
card.flavorText: The Matilda “Frog” was an Australian flamethrower version of the British Matilda II infantry tank, developed for jungle warfare in the Pacific. In 1943, the Australian Army asked for a tank-mounted flame weapon, and Major A.E. Miller helped shape the final design. A prototype was completed in 1944, and production of 25 units was approved. The first tank was ready by July 1944 and was demonstrated to General Thomas Blamey at Monegeetta Proving Grounds. The Frog replaced the Matilda’s 2-pounder gun with a flame projector hidden inside a tube, so the tank still looked much like a normal gun tank. Its fuel and pressure system were carried inside the vehicle rather than in a trailer. The turret held an 80-gallon fuel tank and pressure equipment, which left room for only one man there. Extra fuel tanks could be fitted inside and outside the hull. The flamethrower could fire about 90 yards, but needed around 30 seconds to build pressure between shots. Matilda Frogs were used on Borneo, where they proved effective against fortified Japanese positions.
